left: Second-floor sash lintels at y 22 (x 5, 11, 13, 19, z 19) are not built: the shell closed those cells as brick. The shell should leave them as trim.
The street door's trim surround at x 22 and x 25, y 7..9, z 19 is not built: the shell closed those cells as brick. The shell should leave them as trim.
The roof's dentil row at y 21 z 20 takes the middle glass cells of each oriel's top row (x 8 and 16), so those two panes are smooth stone. The roof part should skip z 20 at y 21 over the oriels.
Rear windows have no sill and no trim lintel. The shell's brick lintel stands above them, and plan gives the rear no sills.
Oriel glass uses explicit pane connection states (east/west true) set in this part. The vocab's oriel() writes plain glass_pane, which would show as thin posts.

waste.what: Worked out which earlier part owned each refused cell (the roof's dentils at y 21 z 20) by probing the built grid with throwaway scripts.
waste.cost: about 3 probe runs and roughly 5 minutes of the 12-minute session
waste.tool: The runParts REFUSED line should name the part that placed the cell (here roof), not only the block id, and mcd could print a one-line 'who owns this cell' for any x,y,z.

waste.what: Oriel glass connection states set by hand: vocab oriel() writes plain glass_pane, so I re-set each row of glass with east/west true.
waste.tool: oriel() should take a glass option that sets pane connections along the wall, the way sashWindow already does.

waste.what: Single doors (rear, keeper, corridor, flat) written cell by cell from B.door, because streetDoor only builds the double street door.
waste.cost: about 12 door calls hand-placed, halves and hinges set by hand
waste.tool: A door(g, x, y0, z, {facing, hinge}) helper in vocab (lower and upper halves, air-checked) would replace the hand-written door() in windows.mjs.

waste.what: Window and door openings laid out by reading plan.md's OPENINGS table and matching them to the shell's air cells by hand.
waste.cost: about 40 cell coordinates worked out and checked against the shell source
waste.tool: A plan-to-coordinates reader for the OPENINGS table, or a shell that writes an 'openings' list the windows part can iterate over.

waste.what: Render tiles labelled front-elevation show the rear (north) face, so I had to find the street face in back-elevation and zoom to check it.
waste.cost: one wasted render read and one zoom
waste.tool: mcd render --front should be documented to name the face it shows, or the street face should get its own label in the tiles.
